answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from a per-identity bond that scales with claimed activity: an operator must lock collateral for every address it keeps live, so cloning one agent into many costs more than the clones can earn back. Reputation is credited only to histories backed by that stake, so a fresh copy starts at zero while carrying real liability. The price of faking depth filters shallow copies out like a reef, and cheap identities sink below the horizon of what counts as real work, deeper than the reach of any ocean of throwaway addresses.
